title: Jason Cohen on strategy, bootstrapping and customer development: lessons from WP Engine and Smart Bear
summary: Jason Cohen explains why you shouldn't set out to bootstrap a billion-dollar company, and how to design a bootstrapped business with recurring value and annual prepay. He also covers strategy as a self-reinforcing set of decisions, running hypothesis-driven customer interviews, and managing executives.

principles.text: Strategy is how you win: a set of decisions that fit together, so copying one piece doesn't copy the system.
principles.quote: strategy is overall how you're going to win.

principles.text: Conflicting advice (niche vs broad) isn't right or wrong. Ask when it applies, then make surrounding decisions that fit.
principles.quote: A better question is when is this advice applicable?

principles.text: Annual prepay lets a bootstrapper fund acquisition with customer cash, removing the marketing budget cap while the channel is profitable.
principles.quote: you went from a marketing budget that was limited to $100 a month or less to unlimited marketing budget

principles.text: Recurring revenue only works if the value is also delivered on a recurring basis, not just billed monthly.
principles.quote: I think one thing people do wrong a lot is they don't deliver value in a recurring pattern as well.

principles.text: Run customer interviews as experiments with hypotheses and open questions. Stop when you stop being surprised.
principles.quote: you do enough of these to where you're not learning anything anymore. You can tell because you're just never surprised.

principles.text: Find the trigger event that makes customers switch, or your marketing is just shouting ads at people.
principles.quote: Whatever that is, you've got to find out what that is. Cuz otherwise, you're just yelling ads at people
